policy: Use a dataset-wide zero-offset fixed scale for PET input and target. Per-image min-max is prohibited for the primary experiment and remains limited to the SAM prior kernel transform. A candidate that is mathematically identical on every training array does not justify duplicate decoder training.
lock_status: DEVELOPMENT CANDIDATE SELECTED, NOT PAPER-LOCKED — no untouched test set is currently registered.

domain_physical_fixed_C.description: A scale constant derived from scanner metadata, a vendor definition, or a simulation definition. This is the only candidate that may be called a physical constant.
domain_physical_fixed_C.eligibility: Unavailable until a traceable physical source is supplied.

train_derived_zero_offset_fixed_C.description: Training-set global maximum, with zero offset and no clipping. This is a data-derived fixed scale, not a physical constant.
train_derived_zero_offset_fixed_C.eligibility: Selected for the development training run because it preserves a common zero and does not clip validation activity.

train_global_minmax_sensitivity.description: Training-set [min,max] affine normalization with clipping to [0,1].
train_global_minmax_sensitivity.eligibility: DIAGNOSTIC ONLY in this study. Both training minima are zero, so it is pixel-identical to train_max_fixed_C on all training arrays and differs only by validation clipping.

per_image_minmax_diagnostic_only.description: Per-image [min,max] normalization computed independently for every image.
per_image_minmax_diagnostic_only.eligibility: DIAGNOSTIC ONLY. It destroys between-case quantitative comparability and is never eligible as the primary PET scale.

forbidden_uses: Per-image min-max as the PET input or target scale.
An arbitrary constant such as 30000 without a recorded source for the ingested representation.
Any validation- or test-derived scale constant.
Training a duplicate global-min-max decoder when its training transform is identical to train_max_fixed_C.

base_yaml_state.reason: The development values are injected into a namespaced generated configuration. The base configuration remains unresolved and cannot be mistaken for a paper-locked run.
